_comment.what: The SideStore source for the iOS client. Paste https://github.com/poalrom/sharepaste/releases/latest/download/sidestore-source.json into SideStore's Sources tab; that URL always redirects to the newest published Release, so the source keeps working without being re-added.
_comment.why it lives in .github: It is release machinery, beside release-body-header.md and scripts/build-latest-json.mjs. Nobody types this path: `publish` uploads the file to the Release under the plain name sidestore-source.json, and that is the copy SideStore reads.
_comment.bundleIdentifier: PLACEHOLDER, and the ticket that owns this file does not close until it is replaced. The identifier below must be the one actually installed on the device, which is NOT com.sharepaste.ios: xtool prefixes its team (XTL-1234.com.sharepaste.ios) and SideStore applies its own scheme. Read it off the device with `ideviceinstaller -l` after SideStore has installed the app once, and commit that value. Get it wrong and SideStore does not offer an update; it offers a fresh install, which lands beside the real app with an empty database while the Pairings sit in the old one.
_comment.why no pipeline check: Comparing this identifier against Info.plist was considered and rejected. The plist holds com.sharepaste.ios and the device holds the rewritten form, so such a check would go green while the real path was broken — it would test that two strings nobody installs agree with each other. What is checked in CI instead is `version` and both downloadURLs against the Release being published, in the `publish` job; the identifier is proved by watching a real v1 to v2 update land in place with the Pairing intact.
_comment.two downloadURLs: ADR 0008 §100-103: SideStore needs the app-level downloadURL/version/size as well as the ones inside versions[]. A file carrying only versions[] is accepted by AltStore and rejected by SideStore.
_comment.size: Bytes of the .ipa, used for the download progress display only. Left at 0 because the value is not known until the artifact is built, and a wrong one costs a progress bar rather than an install.

apps.name: Sharepaste
apps.subtitle: End-to-end encrypted clipboard sync with your own machines.
apps.localizedDescription:
Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted clipboard sync between a person's own machines. A Relay you run yourself stores and fans out ciphertext it can never read; this phone decrypts locally with a key the relay never sees.

Sync is foreground-only: nothing runs while the app is closed. Two Shortcuts actions — Offer and Recall Latest — are the way to use it without opening it.

Unsigned, and signed on your own device by a free Apple Personal Team, which means the installation expires every seven days and SideStore refreshes it.
apps.versionDescription: The first iOS release. Pair with a short code, see the History, Offer and Recall, and drive both verbs from Shortcuts.
